Shares of Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) leaped on Wednesday after the server maker announced preliminary financial results.

Image source: Getty Images.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Supplying AI data centers with the equipment they need

Supermicro expects to report revenue of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion in its fiscal 2027 first quarter, which ended on Sept. 30. That's significantly above management's prior forecast of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion and Wall Street's projections of roughly $15 billion.

The data center infrastructure provider said the stronger-than-expected results were driven by rising demand for its artificial intelligence (AI) platforms.

Additionally, Supermicro expects to report a gross margin of 12% to 12.5%, well above its previous guidance of 10.4% to 10.8%, due to a more favorable customer and product mix.

This improved profitability suggests that robust AI-related demand is enabling computing infrastructure suppliers to charge higher prices for their products.

AI stocks are rallying

The news comes as a welcome relief for investors, and fellow server makers Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise rose in kind.

Many AI stocks have pulled back in recent weeks, due to mounting fears of surging debt levels among data center builders and other technology companies.

Supermicro's results suggest the AI build-out boom may have more room to run. Investors can expect to hear more about management's view of this increasingly important global trend during Supermicro's upcoming earnings call on Nov. 3 at 5:00 p.m. ET.

(Updates with index/price moves, macroeconomic data, and company news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes rose as a rally in SpaceX (SPCX) and Super Micro Computer's (SMCI) shares boosted risk sentiment in growth sectors, while crude oil prices declined.

The Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.2% to 26,739.1, the S&P 500 climbed 0.6% to 7,757.9, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 0.4% to 52,681.9 after midday Wednesday. Technology, industrials, financials, and consumer discretionary topped the gainers. Communication services led decliners.

SpaceX, which also led Nasdaq's gainers, said late Tuesday it swung into the black in Q3 as revenue rose, driven by strong gains in its artificial intelligence and connectivity divisions. Meanwhile, Elon Musk, who heads both SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA), said the duo has formed special committees to evaluate a potential merger.

Super Micro Computer's shares surged 9% after the company reported preliminary fiscal Q1 revenue and margin results above expectations late Tuesday.

Netflix (NFLX) dropped 4.8%, among the worst performers on the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq, after the streaming giant's below-consensus Q4 outlook undermined better-than-expected Q3 earnings.

Seven of the top 10 stocks in a category with market capitalization exceeding $200 billion were from the technology sector, according to data compiled by Finviz. SpaceX topped this list of mega-caps, gaining 8.8%. The iShares PHLX Semiconductor Exchange Traded Fund (SOXX), with about $48.43 billion in assets under management, jumped 2.4% as investors continued to dip their toes back in the AI trade after last week's sharp sell-off.

In energy market news, US commercial crude oil stocks, excluding inventories in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, fell by 3.1 million barrels in the week ended Oct. 16, after an 8.6-million-barrel decrease in the previous week, versus the 340,000-barrel decline expected in a Bloomberg-compiled survey.

The front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract dropped 1.2% to $96.68 per barrel, and global benchmark Brent slipped 0.3% to $108.47 per barrel.

Gold futures edged up 0.2% to $4,150.2, while silver futures slipped 0.5% to $57.70.

In economic news, mortgage applications fell 5.3% in the week ended Oct. 16 amid declines in refinancing activity and new home applications, while borrowers whistled past the first drop in 30-year fixed mortgage rates in two months, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association. This follows a 2.7% decrease in overall activity in the week ended Oct. 9.

Most US Treasury yields fell after midday. The 10-year yield edged 1.3 basis points lower to 5.10%, while the 30-year rate fell 1.6 basis points to 5.41%. The two-year rate was little changed at 4.79%.
